correctness.rationale: The even rectangles give M(x,y)=u(x)+v(y) over F2 with one common flip gauge. For side-preserving permutations, the two differences must be the same constant, which may be 1 only when both permutations have all cycles even. Multiplying the resulting three block counts and averaging yields U_n. For a class swap, choose coordinates so the two successive maps give σ on one shore. The reversed block satisfies M(x,y)=1+M(σy,x), forcing v=u+t and u(σx)=u(x)+1; the gauge leaves 2^{c(σ)} choices when all σ cycles are even. The other blocks exchange, so one must be fixed by (σ,γ²) and determines the other. For γ, each even cycle splits under squaring, and γ² has only even cycles precisely when every γ cycle length is divisible by 4. The two cycle indices are (1−z)^(−2)(1−z²)^(−1) and (1−z⁴)^(−1), giving H_n and E_n. A class 3-cycle cycles all blocks; using cyclic orientations there is no net complement and one block is fixed under conjugate copies of the same permutation. Burnside with multiplicities 1,3,2 then gives V_n and the degree-nine leading coefficient. For any proposed period p not divisible by 4, the progression 0 mod p contains infinite subprogressions in both 0 and 2 mod 4; the two differing polynomial constituents would have to agree identically. The odd/even argument similarly gives minimal period two for U_n.
residual_risks: The finite checks are corroborative; the proof establishes the unbounded statement. The term 'rank-one binary edge block' is not a literal matrix rank bound over F2; the proof uses the verified affine additive form, which can have matrix rank two.

value.rationale: This is a natural finite enumeration for the first number of shores at which the fixed third class under a transposition couples to a pair of exchanged blocks. The exact named and anonymous counts show a qualitative change of least period, rather than just a leading coefficient or a single enumerated case. The fourth-residue term identifies which symmetries cause the change and provides exact benchmarks for this class of finite digraphs.
residual_risks: No extension to unequal or more numerous shores or to arbitrary finite orientations is claimed.
